offense_analyst.prose: LAC is a run-leaning, low-efficiency offense. On early downs it dropbacks on 51.1% of plays [oc1] over 366 plays [oc2], but on third-and-long it throws on 90.9% of snaps [oc3] over 55 plays [oc4], so a long-yardage down is the clearest passing tell. Overall it sits at -10.3 pass rate over expected [oc5], 30th in the league [oc6], and its EPA per play of -0.24 [oc7] ranks 32nd [oc8]. Its pass offense is not built on big plays: explosives come on 6.4% of pass plays [oc9] with an average target depth of 7.8 yards [oc10]. BAL's defense allows explosives on 8.3% of pass plays [oc11], so the matchup is not a bigger-play threat from LAC, and the plan should be to keep the offense on schedule and avoid the long-down pass. On the ground, LAC leans left at 37.7% [oc12] with middle and right each at 31.2% [oc13][oc14]; it runs with a 34.8% success rate [oc15] on 199 designed runs [oc16]. Its play action share is 25.1% of dropbacks [oc17], motion appears on 72.8% of plays [oc18], screens are 10.5% of dropbacks [oc19], and RPOs are rare at 2.8% [oc20]. BAL allows 0.01 EPA per play [oc21], so its defense is near neutral overall. Expect motion before most snaps and watch for play action on early downs.

First, long-yardage downs: LAC throws on 90.9% of third-and-long snaps [mc1] over 55 plays [mc2], so BAL should call coverage that takes away the deep out and rush hard on those downs rather than chase the pass on early downs. Keep max-protect and hot throws ready, and build the protection plan around whoever takes the snaps, since both Jackson and Huntley are out. Third, Henry against LAC's run defense: Henry carries 73.8% of BAL's rushes [mc7] over 237 team rushes [mc8], and LAC allows a 40.4% run success rate [mc9]. Establish the run early to keep LAC's early-down pass tendency in check and to set up play action. Fourth, explosives: LAC allows explosive plays on 9.7% of snaps [mc10], 25th in the league [mc11], so BAL's shot plays should target that gap, but only once the protection is holding.
